rules: Every proven feature has a model or positive witness.
Every accepted boundary has a nearest rejected or malformed witness.
Runtime facts do not imply Android framework or device behavior.
Unknown features never count as a support claim.
Release tier uses selected producer/hardening witnesses, not a blind Cartesian product.

features.obligation: ELF64 little-endian AArch64 ET_DYN identity and bounded load map
Each AArch64 ET_DYN PT_LOAD with p_align greater than one uses a power-of-two alignment and congruent p_offset and p_vaddr residues, including non-page-sized alignment
PT_DYNAMIC and dynamic metadata are mapped and bounded
The narrow HostContext adapter accepts AArch64 RELATIVE/RELR relocation targets in writable load segments and delegates application to the native loader
constraints: AArch64 RELA entries must be NONE or RELATIVE with symbol index zero
RELR targets must be aligned and writable
Dynamic flag entries allow only immediate binding flags
The system loader remains responsible for applying accepted relocations

features.obligation: A valid ET_DYN remains parseable when section headers are absent; program headers remain authoritative
A HostContext AArch64 ET_DYN remains loadable when section headers are absent; program headers and dynamic metadata remain authoritative
constraints: The image must still provide bounded AArch64 PT_LOAD and PT_DYNAMIC program headers
This validates the native adapter slice and does not claim broader loader behavior

features.obligation: A bounded PT_GNU_RELRO program header has a file-backed range inside the AArch64 image with p_memsz >= p_filesz, and the retained image completes HostContext entry dispatch
constraints: The self-test covers only a bounded PT_GNU_RELRO program-header file range and p_memsz >= p_filesz
The unmodified image retaining PT_GNU_RELRO must dispatch through the real adapter with status 23
Memory protection semantics remain delegated to the native system loader; this is validated implementation evidence, not proof of a custom RELRO implementation

features.obligation: The HostContext adapter accepts a PT_GNU_STACK program header when PF_X is clear and rejects an executable PT_GNU_STACK before creating an image handle
constraints: The real fixture must contain PT_GNU_STACK with PF_X clear and must complete HostContext dispatch through the unchanged adapter path
The self-test sets only the PT_GNU_STACK p_flags PF_X bit in one bounded image copy and requires URP_STATUS_UNSUPPORTED with a zero image handle before loading

Memory protection remains delegated to the native system loader for the accepted non-executable GNU_STACK case; this is validated implementation evidence, not proof of custom stack-protection semantics

features.obligation: The release-tier GCC AArch64 PIE witness is built with full GNU RELRO and immediate binding and retains that ELF hardening in the release artifact.
constraints: This is one deliberate release producer/hardening witness, not a compiler/runtime Cartesian product.
The existing gcc-c fixture builder supplies the source and execution path; the release-hardened variant adds -z relro -z now.
The runner readelf oracle requires GNU_RELRO and BIND_NOW before baseline/copy comparison.

features.obligation: AArch64 dynamically linked PIE runs on the recorded native glibc host
AArch64 dynamically linked PIE runs with the recorded musl loader
AArch64 PIE is executed by the pinned bionic linker using a pinned Termux compiler package set whose downloaded artifacts match locked SHA-256 digests.
constraints: The OCI image digest and Termux source revision are pinned.
Clang and every package newly installed to provide its compiler/linker are version- and SHA-256-locked in the manifest and verified before installation.

The Termux package index is used only to locate those locked artifacts; a missing, changed, or additional package fails the lane, while the complete before/after installed package inventories and license identifiers are retained.

features.obligation: Versioned HostContext v1 callbacks and the legacy frame provide immutable AArch64 ET_DYN image loading and explicit entry dispatch for the declared adapter slice; the native adapter enforces image-byte immutability with verified memfd seals before loader handoff.
constraints: The native adapter creates the memfd with MFD_ALLOW_SEALING, adds F_SEAL_WRITE/F_SEAL_SHRINK/F_SEAL_GROW/F_SEAL_SEAL after the complete verified write, verifies F_GET_SEALS, and fails closed before dlopen when any seal operation is unavailable or incomplete.
No PT_INTERP or DT_NEEDED semantics; constructor/destructor tags use the separate runtime.host-context.constructor-destructor rejection boundary
RPATH/RUNPATH tags use the separate runtime.host-context.path-search rejection boundary
Dynamic flags are limited to immediate binding flags; runtime.host-context.unsupported-relocation-table is the dedicated rejection boundary for unsupported relocation-table tags
Only checked AArch64 RELATIVE/RELR relocation targets are accepted; application and memory protection are delegated to the recorded native system loader

features.obligation: HostContext frame v2 carries the ABI, required capabilities, and bounded entry symbol through one frame-relative layout and dispatches the declared entry without a temporary executable path
constraints: The legacy v1 wrapper-absolute offset remains unchanged
v2 reserved fields must be zero and unknown ABI or capability bits are rejected before image loading
Entry and source names are bounded strict UTF-8 values without path components; ordinary standalone PIE inputs are not implicitly HostContext images
The production managed pack path intentionally emits legacy v1 for the legacy launcher; HostContext v2 production-pack integration is a separate unknown migration boundary.

features.obligation: The production managed pack command can select a HostContext entry image and a compatible v2-capable launcher without forcing a v2 frame into the legacy v1 launcher.
features.nextEvidence: Add a production HostContext pack option that accepts a declared HostContext entry-image adapter and a v2-capable launcher, then retain a managed pack/dispatch oracle proving v2 metadata, immutable in-process handoff, and entry dispatch. Until that adapter, v2-capable launcher, and oracle exist, ElfPackService must keep emitting v1 to the legacy launcher and this row remains unknown.

features.obligation: The pinned native ARM64 Termux userspace can exercise HostContext v2 immutable image loading and entry dispatch without an executable temporary pathname
features.nextEvidence: Run a dedicated bionic HostContext/package oracle: build or provide a HostContext v2 entry image, execute it through the /system/bin/linker64-compatible adapter with immutable sealed-image evidence, and retain .artifacts/bionic/c-termux-bionic-pie/host-context plus linker, kernel, page-size, package-lock, and no-fallback facts. The absent HostContext oracle keeps this row unknown.

features.obligation: Recovered bytes reach the runtime without an executable temporary pathname
An interpreter outside the declared AArch64 host runtimes is refused
features.reason: The current no-path contract does not define dependency resolution for arbitrary interpreters.

features.obligation: The HostContext v1 adapter rejects PT_TLS before creating an image handle because its system-loader contract does not define TLS or thread lifetime semantics
features.reason: HostContext v1 does not define TLS module allocation, per-thread initialization, TLS relocation models, thread creation/reentrancy, or TLS teardown relative to release_image; dlopen acceptance alone is not a compatibility proof.
constraints: The unchanged entry fixture is the positive HostContext dispatch baseline.
A structurally bounded PT_TLS mutation is rejected with URP_STATUS_UNSUPPORTED and a zero image handle.
A PT_TLS mutation with p_filesz greater than p_memsz is rejected with URP_STATUS_LOAD_FAILED before any loader handoff.
No positive TLS HostContext fixture or support claim exists until the Host Contract defines TLS and thread lifetime semantics.

features.obligation: The HostContext v1 adapter rejects PT_GNU_PROPERTY BTI/PAC/instruction-property metadata before creating an image handle because its system-loader contract defines no property negotiation or instruction-state semantics
features.reason: HostContext v1 and the current system-loader adapter define no GNU property negotiation or BTI/PAC/instruction-state obligations; dlopen acceptance of a property note alone is not a compatibility proof.
constraints: The unchanged entry fixture is the positive HostContext dispatch baseline.
A bounded PT_LOAD-covered metadata segment mutation to PT_GNU_PROPERTY is rejected with URP_STATUS_UNSUPPORTED and a zero image handle before loader handoff.
No positive GNU property HostContext fixture or support claim exists until the Host Contract defines property negotiation and BTI/PAC/instruction-state semantics.

features.obligation: The HostContext v1 system-loader adapter rejects DT_NEEDED, DT_AUXILIARY, and DT_FILTER dependency metadata before dependency resolution or image creation
features.reason: HostContext v1 and the current system-loader adapter define no dependency-resolution, search-path, symbol-scope, or dependency-lifetime semantics; a loader resolving a library is not a compatibility proof.
constraints: The unchanged non-dependency entry fixture remains the positive HostContext dispatch baseline.

Each bounded dynamic-table mutation changes only one of DT_NEEDED, DT_AUXILIARY, or DT_FILTER, is rejected with URP_STATUS_UNSUPPORTED and a zero image handle before loader handoff, and preserves every surrounding byte.
No positive dependency-bearing HostContext fixture or support claim exists until the Host Contract defines dependency resolution, search paths, symbol scope, and dependency lifetime.

features.obligation: The HostContext v1 system-loader adapter rejects DT_INIT, DT_FINI, DT_INIT_ARRAY, DT_FINI_ARRAY, DT_INIT_ARRAYSZ, DT_FINI_ARRAYSZ, DT_PREINIT_ARRAY, and DT_PREINIT_ARRAYSZ before constructor or destructor execution and image-handle creation
features.reason: HostContext v1 and the current system-loader adapter define no constructor/destructor ordering, callback or reentrancy behavior, teardown, or lifecycle ownership semantics for in-process images; loader execution alone is not a compatibility proof.
constraints: The unchanged non-lifecycle entry fixture remains the positive HostContext dispatch baseline.

Each bounded dynamic-table mutation changes only one DT_NULL tag, preserves surrounding bytes, initializes a nonzero sentinel handle, and must return URP_STATUS_UNSUPPORTED with a zero handle before loader handoff.
Unsupported relocation-table tags use the separate runtime.host-context.unsupported-relocation-table rejection boundary and are not part of this feature.
No positive constructor/destructor HostContext fixture or support claim exists until ordering, callback/reentrancy, teardown, and lifecycle ownership semantics are defined by the Host Contract.

features.obligation: The HostContext v1 system-loader adapter rejects DT_RPATH and DT_RUNPATH dynamic path-search metadata before path search or image-handle creation
features.reason: HostContext v1 and the current system-loader adapter define no dynamic path-search roots, ordering, or precedence semantics for in-process images; loader path resolution alone is not a compatibility proof.
constraints: The unchanged non-path-search entry fixture remains the positive HostContext dispatch baseline.

Each bounded dynamic-table mutation changes only one DT_NULL tag, preserves surrounding bytes, initializes a nonzero sentinel handle, and must return URP_STATUS_UNSUPPORTED with a zero handle before loader handoff.
Constructor/destructor lifecycle metadata and runtime.host-context.unsupported-relocation-table remain separate rejection boundaries.

features.obligation: The HostContext v1 system-loader adapter rejects DT_TEXTREL writable-text relocation metadata before writable-text relocation or image-handle creation
features.reason: HostContext v1 and the current system-loader adapter define no writable-text relocation or W^X/protection semantics for in-process images; loader acceptance alone is not a compatibility proof.
constraints: The unchanged non-text-relocation entry fixture remains the positive HostContext dispatch baseline.

A bounded dynamic-table mutation changes only one DT_NULL tag to DT_TEXTREL, preserves surrounding bytes, initializes a nonzero sentinel handle, and must return URP_STATUS_UNSUPPORTED with a zero handle before loader handoff.
AArch64 RELATIVE/RELR relocation acceptance and application delegation remain the separate validated elf.relocation.aarch64-relative feature.
Unsupported relocation-table tags use the separate runtime.host-context.unsupported-relocation-table rejection boundary.
No positive text-relocation HostContext fixture or support claim exists until writable-text relocation and W^X/protection semantics are defined by the Host Contract.

features.obligation: The HostContext v1 system-loader adapter rejects DT_REL, DT_RELSZ, DT_RELENT, DT_JMPREL, DT_PLTRELSZ, and DT_PLTREL relocation-table metadata before relocation processing or image-handle creation
features.reason: HostContext v1 and the current system-loader adapter define only the checked AArch64 RELATIVE/RELR relocation path; legacy REL and PLT relocation-table semantics are not defined, so loader acceptance alone is not a compatibility proof.
constraints: The unchanged RELATIVE/RELR entry fixture remains the positive HostContext dispatch baseline.

Each bounded dynamic-table mutation changes only one DT_NULL tag, preserves surrounding bytes, initializes a nonzero sentinel handle, and must return URP_STATUS_UNSUPPORTED with a zero handle before loader handoff.
The validated elf.relocation.aarch64-relative feature covers only checked AArch64 RELATIVE/RELR relocation targets; no broader relocation-table support is claimed.
No positive unsupported-relocation-table HostContext fixture or support claim exists until the Host Contract defines the required relocation-table semantics.

features.obligation: arm64-v8a JNI library loads through the recorded x86_64 Android native bridge
